description: Stack E044's 28 px middle stage onto the E045 tip. This combines a near-miss with a margin that can absorb it. The tip is E045 (commit bfcff33): bs 1536, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5 then 32 px, 6.75 epochs total, SGD-group lr x1.5, head lr x2 with wd halved, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, brightness/contrast jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. Make one change, ported from E044 (drafts/E044_res3_submission.py): 24 px for epochs 0-1.5 as now, then 28 px whole images (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip, translate and jitter) for epochs 1.5-3.0, then 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs. Total epochs, bs and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged, so the sample stream and lr values are identical to E045. A switch that falls mid-epoch uses the first part of that epoch's permutation at the old resolution and the rest at the new one. The 28 px graph's final pool is F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to its final map (expect 3x3). Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (E009). In build(), warm up the 28 px train step without whitening-bias grad at bs 1536, plus every partial-batch shape at both switches, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Check that total build time stays under ~450 s (E044 took 232 s for 6 variants). If I060's 20 px first stage was kept first, apply this change to that commit instead and leave its first stage alone. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.
